title: N159W GeMS/GSAOI Image
caption: The N159W field in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This near-infrared view from Gemini South shows the N159W field in the Large Magellanic Cloud. It was made with the GeMS adaptive optics system and the GSAOI camera, and it resolves stars as finely as about 0.09 arcseconds.

The Large Magellanic Cloud is a small companion galaxy of the Milky Way, visible from the Southern Hemisphere. Adaptive optics measures how turbulence in Earth's atmosphere distorts incoming light and corrects it on the fly with a deformable mirror, letting a telescope on the ground produce much sharper images than it otherwise could.

Near-infrared light, just beyond the red end of what our eyes can see, passes through dust more easily than visible light. The picture combines three filters, J, H and Ks, with 25 minutes of exposure through each, and spans 1.5 arcminutes of sky. Travis Rector of the University of Alaska Anchorage produced the color composite.

understand.summary: A near-infrared image from GeMS/GSAOI on Gemini South through J, H and Ks filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, so the colors here are a translation of light we cannot see.
